The same record sets the actual searched range to 46 through 60 characters, and carries its own flag, set to false, saying the predicted spacing falls outside that range.

questions.changes: The study's central negative result about a repeating pattern would describe a wavelength nobody expected to matter, while the wavelength the theory actually predicted, 140 characters, was never checked at all.

questions.question: Is a value that beats only 54 percent of randomly relabeled control runs meaningfully different from an ordinary, typical noise value, rather than simply short of the significance cutoff?

findings.crux: Selection bias would need to produce a falsely extreme (near rank 1 or rank 200) statistic to manufacture apparent significance; the committed rank is 109/200 (match rate 0.54229), i.e. almost exactly the 50th-percentile median of the null/shuffle distribution — already an unremarkable draw, not an extreme one that selection could have manufactured.

findings.confound: readout artifact — the possibility that the pattern-strength metric's own readout mechanism (not a genuine repeating structure) governs where the measured value falls relative to shuffled controls
findings.crux: The claim is itself a null statement ("this value is ordinary noise, not a near-miss"). The committed numbers (rank 109/200, match rate 0.54229) place the measured value almost exactly at the 50th percentile of the 200 shuffle-control distribution -- precisely where a value produced by the same readout process acting on pure noise would land. This is fully consistent with a readout that carries no real repeating-pattern signal (i.e., it IS the explanation the claim asserts), not a fact that needs to be ruled out.

findings.confound: regime specificity
findings.crux: Whether the near-median rank (109/200, match rate 0.54229) reported for the single arm-ripple_vs_shuffle_endpoint-4_stage-endpoints record is representative of match rates/ranks across the other endpoint indices, stages, and arms in the same sweep, or whether this is a comparatively unremarkable-looking regime cherry-picked among others that might show much higher (near-significant) or much lower match rates.

findings.confound: construct validity
findings.crux: Rank 109/200 (54.229% match rate) places the measured value almost exactly at the median of the null (shuffle-control) distribution, not near its tail — this is what "indistinguishable from typical noise" looks like numerically. The claim under audit is itself a null/negative claim (the statistic is not meaningfully different from an ordinary noise value), and the cited evidence is the direct, literal confirmation of that null, not a confound artifact that could be masking a real effect. So EXPLAINS here means the confound-mechanism (percentile framing vs. cutoff framing) IS the substance of the claim holding: recharacterizing "108/200 controls beaten" as "sits in the middle of the noise pile" rather than "just below threshold" is the same fact restated, and both framings agree the value is unremarkable.

findings.confound: Scale incomparability would require comparing quantities on different, non-commensurable units/scales. Here the reported number (rank 109/200, match rate 0.54229) is a percentile position of the pattern-strength statistic against 200 control runs built from the identical statistic/pipeline (random relabeling), which is scale-free by construction — there is no differently-scaled quantity being compared.
findings.crux: The decisive fact is that the cited statistic (0.54229 match rate, rank 109/200) is itself a percentile/rank against an empirical null built from the same measure, not a raw value compared across differing units — so scale incomparability has no purchase on this particular number.

findings.confound: noise floor
findings.crux: Rank 109/200 (match rate 0.54229) places the measured value almost exactly at the 50th percentile of the shuffle-control distribution — i.e., it looks like a typical, unremarkable draw from the noise distribution itself, not a value sitting just below a significance threshold.

findings.confound: Ceiling/floor effect: worry that a metric saturating at a boundary (floor near 0 or ceiling) would make rank-based comparisons against shuffled controls meaningless/artifactual.
findings.crux: A floor/ceiling saturation artifact would manifest as an extreme percentile (rank near 1/200 or 200/200, ties at a boundary value), but the committed rank is 109/200 (match rate 0.54229) — squarely mid-distribution, which is the signature of an ordinary noise draw, not of metric saturation at a bound.

findings.confound: single-case overfit: the worry that the measured pattern-strength (0.000012449) reflects fitting/selecting on one specific run/case rather than a stable, generalizable signal, which could make its true relationship to noise unclear or its rank artifact-driven.
findings.crux: The claim being audited is a null claim ("this value is ordinary noise, not a near-miss"), and it is settled directly by the committed rank statistic itself: the measured value ranks 109th of 200 random-relabeling controls (match rate 0.54229), i.e. almost exactly the 50th-55th percentile of the null distribution. This is a direct distributional comparison against 200 independently generated shuffle nulls -- not a single case being over-interpreted. Single-case overfit as a confound would apply if the pattern-strength number had been computed/selected on one favorable instance with no proper null reference, making its apparent (non-)significance unreliable; here the opposite is true -- the number's ordinariness is demonstrated by its position within a 200-run null distribution, which is exactly the kind of evidence that neutralizes single-case-overfit concerns rather than needing to be explained by them.
